expected_vs_observed: Expected (candidate, loop_risk 0.2): a cheap close was possible after run 008. Observed: the cheap tier's implementation satisfied the oracle but its own tests failed (declared checks 0/1/0), so the router set it aside (stash f55b2863) and the fallback closed the task (deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud, 52 turns, 43,932 output tokens, 321.0 s). Whole route: 76 turns, 59,053 output tokens, 422.59 s of router wall; the closing attempt alone would understate it by 24 turns, 15,121 tokens and 101.6 s.

Expected: an observation of path B on real work. Observed: the first launch (Workflow wf_a8a8268c, 28.9 s) was killed by the harness because the relay read the output file with cat instead of calling the wait command and then ended its turn; the router had only announced its run (state: tree_check done, baseline in progress) and no worker change reached the tree. The second launch (wf_eae63803, 578 s) went as installed: background launch, eight wait calls printing NOT_FINAL, then COLLECTED with the run bound. Path B is exercised on an ordinary task.

Expected: one verdict. Observed: the first verdict (glm53_flash, 101.1 s) was OBJECT because the fallback worker left an empty untracked .run_checks.sh it could not delete and said so in its answer; the driver removed that file (driver_intervention.txt), re-ran the declared checks, and a second verdict on the cleaned tree (glm53_flash, 98.5 s) was ACCEPT. Both verdict receipts are kept.

reasons: Every criterion has a passing check re-run by the driver at the obtained revision in an isolated worktree, with the outputs kept as files that carry the exit line rule 1 reads

Costs: costs.route is the whole route from the receipt (both attempts, the set-aside one included) and costs.measured the closing attempt; verifier wall is the second verdict's; the first verdict, the killed first launch, the Workflow relays and the driver's time are in the README; money is unknown

notes: Run 009: the record carries whole-route costs bound to the receipt (schema 0.2, rules 5 and 6). This is the first 0.2 record. One driver intervention on the tree (a stray empty file removed) and one relay deviation on the first launch are recorded, not hidden.
